questions.text: How many cantons are named in the first article of Switzerland's federal constitution?
questions.fact: Article 1 of the 1999 constitution names all 26 cantons, from Zurich to Jura.

questions.text: How many US states share a border with Canada, counting borders that run through lakes?
questions.fact: The 13 include Alaska, plus Ohio and Pennsylvania, whose borders with Canada run through Lake Erie.

questions.text: How big is Greenland, in thousands of square kilometres (km²)?
questions.fact: Greenland covers 2,166,086 km², and about 81% of that lies under its ice sheet.

questions.text: How many stars are on the flag of Brazil?
questions.fact: Each star stands for one of the 26 states or the Federal District, making 27.

questions.text: How high does Uluru rise above the surrounding plain, in metres?
questions.fact: Uluru stands 348 m high, taller than the Eiffel Tower, and it is 9.4 km around its base.

questions.text: In what year did an international conference choose Greenwich as the prime meridian?
questions.fact: Delegates from 25 nations met in Washington, DC, in 1884; the vote for Greenwich was 22 to 1, with 2 abstaining.

questions.text: How much does one cubic metre of solid gold weigh, in kilograms?
questions.fact: Gold's density is 19,300 kg per cubic metre (19.3 g/cm³), over 19 times that of water.

questions.text: What depth did the Soviet Kola Superdeep Borehole reach in 1989, in metres?
questions.fact: The scientific hole on Russia's Kola Peninsula reached 12,262 m (40,230 ft) in 1989, a little over 12 km straight down.

questions.text: At sea level, at what temperature does pure ethanol, the alcohol in drinks, boil, in °C?
questions.fact: Ethanol boils at about 78 °C, well below water, which is why alcohol can be separated by distilling.

questions.text: At what temperature does pure table salt (sodium chloride) melt, in °C?
questions.fact: Pure sodium chloride melts at 801 °C (1,474 °F), several times hotter than a kitchen oven gets.

questions.text: What is standard air pressure at sea level, in hectopascals (millibars), to the nearest whole number?
questions.fact: One standard atmosphere is defined as 101,325 pascals, which is 1,013.25 hectopascals.

questions.text: In what year was Dolly the sheep, the first mammal cloned from an adult cell, born?
questions.fact: Dolly was born on 5 July 1996 in Scotland; the world heard about her in February 1997.

questions.text: How many Earth days does Venus take to spin once on its axis?
questions.fact: Venus spins backwards once every 243 Earth days, which is longer than its 225-day year.

questions.text: On average, how far is the Moon from Earth, in thousands of kilometres?
questions.fact: The Moon's average distance is about 384,400 km; its light takes just over a second to reach us.

questions.text: How many hours did the Apollo 11 mission last, from launch to splashdown?
questions.fact: Apollo 11 lasted 195 hours, 18 minutes and 35 seconds, ending in the Pacific near the ship USS Hornet.

questions.text: How many full days did cosmonaut Valeri Polyakov spend in space on his 1994-95 flight to the Mir station?
questions.fact: Polyakov was up for 437 days and 18 hours, circling Earth about 7,075 times.

questions.text: How heavy was Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite, launched in 1957, to the nearest kilogram?
questions.fact: The polished metal ball, 58 cm across, weighed 83.6 kg and took about 98 minutes to go once around the Earth.

questions.text: In what year did a Space Shuttle first fly into space?
questions.fact: Columbia launched on 12 April 1981 with John Young and Robert Crippen, landing 54.5 hours later.

questions.text: How many teeth does an adult dog have?
questions.fact: Adult dogs have 42 teeth; adult humans have 32 and adult cats 30.

questions.text: What is the longest life cycle of North America's periodical cicadas, in years?
questions.fact: Three species come up every 17 years and four every 13; both are prime numbers.

questions.text: Each of the six rotating lists of Atlantic storm names has how many names?
questions.fact: Names starting with Q, U, X, Y and Z are left out, so each list uses 21 letters of the alphabet.

questions.text: In 2022 a young bar-tailed godwit flew non-stop from Alaska to Tasmania. About how far, in kilometres?
questions.fact: The bird flew about 13,560 km (8,425 miles) in 11 days without stopping.

questions.text: Up to how many degrees can an owl turn its head in either direction?
questions.fact: Owls can turn their heads up to about 270°, helped by blood pools that keep the brain supplied.

questions.text: In what year was a living coelacanth, a fish thought long extinct, found off South Africa?
questions.fact: Museum curator Marjorie Courtenay-Latimer spotted it in a trawler's catch near East London in December 1938.

questions.text: How many passengers sailed to America on the Mayflower in 1620, not counting the crew?
questions.fact: 102 passengers crowded onto a ship only about 27 m long, plus its crew.

questions.text: How many countries were founding members of the United Nations in 1945?
questions.fact: 50 countries signed the UN Charter in San Francisco on 26 June 1945; Poland signed later as the 51st.

questions.text: How long was the full Berlin Wall border around West Berlin, in kilometres?
questions.fact: The border fortifications ran 155 km around West Berlin; about 43 km of them split the city itself.

questions.text: How many days did Gandhi's Salt March of 1930 last?
questions.fact: The march ran from 12 March to 6 April 1930, ending at Dandi, where Gandhi made salt from seawater.

questions.text: In what year was the Rosetta Stone found?
questions.fact: French soldiers found it in 1799 while rebuilding a fort near Rashid (Rosetta) in Egypt.

questions.text: The University of Bologna dates its founding to what year?
questions.fact: Bologna's own history page gives 1088 as the university's conventional founding date.

questions.text: Louis XIV of France reigned for how many years?
questions.fact: He became king in 1643 aged 4 and reigned until 1715: 72 years and 110 days.

questions.text: How old was Pelé when he played in, and won, his first World Cup final?
questions.fact: Pelé was 17 years and 249 days old and scored twice as Brazil beat Sweden 5-2 in 1958.

questions.text: How many grandchildren did Queen Victoria have?
questions.fact: Victoria had 9 children and 42 grandchildren, many of whom married into Europe's royal families.

questions.text: How old was Alexander the Great when he became king of Macedon?
questions.fact: Born in 356 BC, Alexander took the throne in 336 BC, succeeding his father, Philip II.

questions.text: How old was Edmund Hillary when he reached the top of Mount Everest?
questions.fact: Hillary, born on 20 July 1919, reached the summit with Tenzing Norgay at about 11:30 on 29 May 1953.

questions.text: In what year did Marco Polo get back to Venice after his travels in Asia?
questions.fact: Marco Polo left Venice in 1271 and returned in 1295, after 24 years away.

questions.text: How heavy is the shot in the men's shot put, in grams?
questions.fact: The men's shot weighs 7.26 kg (16 lb); the women's weighs 4 kg.

questions.text: How high is the playing surface of a table tennis table above the floor, in centimetres?
questions.fact: The table top is 76 cm above the floor, and the net is 15.25 cm high.

questions.text: How many balls are on the table, cue ball included, at the start of a frame of snooker?
questions.fact: A frame starts with 15 reds, 6 colours and the white cue ball.

questions.text: How many jumps does a runner clear in a 3,000 m steeplechase, water jumps included?
questions.fact: Runners clear 28 barriers and 7 water jumps in a 3,000 m steeplechase.

questions.text: How long is a tennis court, baseline to baseline, in feet?
questions.fact: The court is 78 ft (23.77 m) long; a singles court is 27 ft wide.

questions.text: In what year was the first Tour de France held?
questions.fact: The 1903 race had six stages covering 2,428 km and was organised by the newspaper L'Auto.

questions.text: When the audio CD was standardised, how many minutes of music was it designed to hold?
questions.fact: The 1980 Red Book standard gave a CD 74 minutes, long enough, the story goes, for Beethoven's Ninth.

questions.text: How many prelude-and-fugue pairs are in Bach's 'Well-Tempered Clavier', both books together?
questions.fact: Each book has a prelude and fugue in all 24 major and minor keys, making 48 pairs.

questions.text: How many Broadway performances did 'The Phantom of the Opera' give before it closed in 2023?
questions.fact: The Broadway run opened in January 1988 and ended at the Majestic Theatre on 16 April 2023.

questions.text: John Cage's 'As Slow as Possible' began playing on a church organ in Germany in 2001. How many years should it last?
questions.fact: The Halberstadt performance began in 2001 and is due to end in 2640; one chord can sound for years before the next change.

questions.text: In what year was the first Eurovision Song Contest held?
questions.fact: Seven countries took part in Lugano, Switzerland, in 1956, each with two songs.

questions.text: Across its eight seasons, how many episodes did 'Game of Thrones' have?
questions.fact: Game of Thrones ran on HBO from 2011 to 2019, with 73 episodes over eight seasons.

questions.text: How many episodes of 'Breaking Bad' were made in its five seasons?
questions.fact: Breaking Bad ran from 2008 to 2013, with 62 episodes over five seasons.

questions.text: How tall is an Oscar statuette, to the nearest centimetre?
questions.fact: The Academy gives it as 13½ inches (34.3 cm) tall and 8½ lb; the film reel it stands on has five spokes.

questions.text: The electronic TV system that won the BBC's 1936 trial drew its picture with how many lines?
questions.fact: Marconi-EMI's 405-line system beat Baird's 240-line system in trials at Alexandra Palace, London.

questions.text: In what year was the first Academy Awards ceremony held?
questions.fact: The first ceremony, on 16 May 1929 at the Hollywood Roosevelt Hotel, honoured films of 1927 and 1928.

questions.text: In what year was 'Raja Harishchandra', often called India's first full-length feature film, released?
questions.fact: Dadasaheb Phalke's silent film 'Raja Harishchandra' came out in 1913.

questions.text: How many sonnets were in the 1609 first edition of Shakespeare's 'Sonnets'?
questions.fact: The publisher Thomas Thorpe printed all 154 sonnets in a small book in 1609.

questions.text: How many lines of verse are in Dante's 'Divine Comedy'?
questions.fact: They fill 100 cantos: an opening canto plus 33 in each of Inferno, Purgatorio and Paradiso.

questions.text: How many chapters are in Jane Austen's 'Pride and Prejudice'?
questions.fact: Pride and Prejudice (1813) has 61 chapters; it first came out in three volumes.

questions.text: In what year was Mary Shelley's 'Frankenstein' first published?
questions.fact: Frankenstein first appeared, without the author's name, in three volumes in 1818; Shelley revised it in 1831.

questions.text: In what year was Chinua Achebe's novel 'Things Fall Apart' published?
questions.fact: Things Fall Apart, published in 1958, was Achebe's first novel.

questions.text: How many tonnes does the metal frame of the Eiffel Tower weigh?
questions.fact: The iron frame weighs 7,300 tonnes; with everything else, the whole tower is about 10,100 tonnes.

questions.text: How tall is the copper Statue of Liberty, from its base to the torch, not counting the pedestal, in metres?
questions.fact: The statue is 151 ft 1 in (46 m) tall; standing on its pedestal and foundation, the torch is 93 m up.

questions.text: How tall is Michelangelo's 'David', including its carved base, in centimetres?
questions.fact: David stands 5.17 m with its base and weighs about 5,560 kg; it was unveiled in Florence in 1504.

questions.text: How many steps climb each of the four staircases of El Castillo at Chichén Itzá?
questions.fact: Four stairways of 91 steps make 364; add the top platform and you get 365, one for each day of the year.

questions.text: In what year was the 'Mona Lisa' stolen from the Louvre?
questions.fact: Vincenzo Peruggia took it on 21 August 1911; it was found in Florence in 1913.

questions.text: In what year was the Sydney Opera House opened?
questions.fact: Queen Elizabeth II opened it on 20 October 1973; Jørn Utzon's design had won a competition in 1957.

questions.text: Under EU rules, 'chocolate' must contain at least what percentage of total dry cocoa solids?
questions.fact: EU Directive 2000/36/EC sets at least 35% total dry cocoa solids for products sold as 'chocolate'.

questions.text: Pure capsaicin, the chemical that makes chillies hot, rates how many million Scoville heat units?
questions.fact: Pure capsaicin rates 16,000,000 Scoville heat units. The scale is named after the US pharmacist Wilbur Scoville.

questions.text: Under EU rules, a 'Pizza Napoletana' bakes on an oven floor at about what temperature, in °C?
questions.fact: The rules set the oven floor at about 485 °C and the dome at about 430 °C, baking for 60 to 90 seconds.

questions.text: Under the EU's 2008 egg rules, a best-before date can be at most how many days after laying?
questions.fact: Regulation (EC) No 589/2008 fixes the best-before date at no more than 28 days after the egg was laid.

questions.text: In what year was Coca-Cola first sold?
questions.fact: The first glass was sold on 8 May 1886 at Jacobs' Pharmacy in Atlanta, Georgia.

questions.text: In what year was the first Michelin Guide published?
questions.fact: About 35,000 copies were given away free in France in 1900, when the country had fewer than 3,000 cars.

questions.text: How many letters does the standard Hawaiian alphabet have?
questions.fact: Hawaiian uses 13 letters: 5 vowels, 7 consonants and the ʻokina, which marks a glottal stop.

questions.text: The lung-disease word often called the longest in English dictionaries has how many letters?
questions.fact: 'Pneumonoultramicroscopicsilicovolcanoconiosis' has 45 letters; it was made up in 1935 as a puzzle.

questions.text: How many words are in the 'Basic English' list drawn up by C. K. Ogden in 1930?
questions.fact: Ogden's Basic English (1930) used just 850 core words to cover everyday English.

questions.text: The Kangxi Dictionary of 1716 lists how many Chinese characters, in thousands?
questions.fact: The Kangxi Dictionary, finished in 1716 for the Kangxi Emperor, lists 47,035 characters.

questions.text: In what year did Noah Webster publish 'An American Dictionary of the English Language'?
questions.fact: Webster's 'An American Dictionary of the English Language' came out in 1828.

questions.text: How many tiles are in a standard double-six set of dominoes?
questions.fact: A double-six set has 28 tiles, with 168 pips in total.

questions.text: How many points (line crossings) are on a standard full-size Go board?
questions.fact: A full Go board has 19 × 19 lines, giving 361 points; sets have 181 black and 180 white stones.

questions.text: How many millilitres are in a UK (imperial) pint, to the nearest whole number?
questions.fact: A UK pint is exactly 568.26125 ml; a US pint is smaller, at about 473 ml.

questions.text: How many litres are in one barrel of oil, the industry's standard unit, to the nearest whole number?
questions.fact: An oil barrel is 42 US gallons, which is 158.987 litres.

questions.text: How many milligrams are in one metric carat, the unit used to weigh gems?
questions.fact: The metric carat was fixed at 200 mg in 1907, so a one-carat diamond weighs 0.2 g.

questions.text: In what year did Robert Recorde first print the equals sign (=)?
questions.fact: Recorde used it in 'The Whetstone of Witte' (1557), as "noe 2 thynges can be moare equalle".

questions.text: How tall is the Hoover Dam, from foundation rock to the roadway on top, in metres?
questions.fact: Hoover Dam is 726.4 ft (221.3 m) tall from its foundation rock to the roadway on its crest.

questions.text: What did Motorola's DynaTAC 8000X, the first handheld mobile phone on sale, cost in the US in 1983, in dollars?
questions.fact: The DynaTAC 8000X cost $3,995 in 1983; it gave 30 minutes of talk time and took 10 hours to charge.

questions.text: How many Concorde airliners were built in total?
questions.fact: 20 Concordes were built, counting test aircraft; 14 of them flew in airline service.

questions.text: How far did the Wright brothers' first powered flight in 1903 travel, in feet?
questions.fact: Orville flew 120 ft in 12 seconds; the best flight that day went 852 ft in 59 seconds.

questions.text: In what year did Ray Tomlinson send the first email between two computers on the ARPANET?
questions.fact: Tomlinson's 1971 program used the @ sign to separate the user's name from the computer's.

questions.text: In what year did Samuel Morse send his famous telegraph message from Washington to Baltimore?
questions.fact: On 24 May 1844 Morse sent the words 'What hath God wrought' along the line from Washington to Baltimore.
